definition_zh: 意外地；出乎意料地；没想到地；突然地
definition_en: in a way that nobody planned for or thought likely
core_image: 还没到门口，人就先一步出现了
scene: 本该下周到的包裹，第二天一早就放在了门口，她连睡衣都没换就笑了。 The parcel arrived unexpectedly.
sceneCN: 这里 unexpectedly 是「意外地」（第 1 个义项：出乎意料）；句意为包裹意外地到了。人先于预期出现的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 副词去掉 -ly 的形容词形式，义为「意外的」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「意外性」
词族核心动词，义为「期待；预料」
肯定形式加 -ly 的副词，义为「如预料地」

senses.title: In a way that was not planned
senses.definition: in a way that nobody had planned for or believed likely
senses.definitionCN: 以没有人计划过、也不认为会发生的方式
senses.example: The meeting ended unexpectedly early and everyone went home by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 会议结束得出奇地早，中午大家就各自回家了。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the negative prefix of the adjective and simply says how the surprise happened.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词保留了形容词的否定前缀，只是把「意外」这件事说成发生的方式。

senses.title: Without warning
senses.definition: used when something happens with no sign beforehand
senses.definitionCN: 形容某事发生前毫无迹象
senses.example: The lights went out unexpectedly in the middle of the film.
senses.exampleCN: 电影放到一半，灯毫无预告地灭了。
senses.why: No expectation means no warning, so the adverb often means simply suddenly.
senses.whyCN: 没有预期也就没有预告，因此这个副词常常就相当于「突然」。

senses.title: Modifying a degree: surprisingly high or low
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say the degree is surprising
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，说明程度令人惊讶
senses.example: The new engine is unexpectedly quiet on the motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机在高速上出奇地安静。
senses.why: A degree that was not guessed can be attached to the verb like any other adverb of manner.
senses.whyCN: 没被猜到的程度，可以和别的方式副词一样挂在形容词前。

senses.title: Behaving in an unforeseen way
senses.definition: used of people who act in a manner others did not expect
senses.definitionCN: 形容人的举动与旁人的预期不符
senses.example: He reacted unexpectedly, laughing at news that should have hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 他的反应出人意料，对着本该伤人的消息笑出声来。
senses.why: Behaviour that escapes prediction is judged from outside, which is exactly what an adverb marks.
senses.whyCN: 逃出预期的行为总由旁观者来评判，而副词正是这种评判的标记。

senses.title: Phrased to open a sentence
senses.definition: often placed at the start of a clause to comment on the whole news
senses.definitionCN: 常放在句首，对整句内容作评论
senses.example: Unexpectedly, the train left on time.
senses.exampleCN: 出乎意料的是，火车准点开走了。
senses.why: An adverb that judges an event can stand outside the clause and set the tone for it.
senses.whyCN: 一个评判事件的副词可以站到句子外面，为整句定调。

intro.en: The word is a chain of small parts: prefix, verb, participle ending, and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词是一串小部件的接续：前缀、动词、分词词尾，再加副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Exspectare meant to look out for, from ex- and spectare, to look.
items.cn: exspectare 意为「向外张望」，由 ex- 与 spectare（看）构成。

items.en: French expecter carried the sense of waiting for something.
items.cn: 法语 expecter 带有「等候某事」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as expect and later used it for predicting.
items.cn: 英语借入动词作 expect，后来用以表示预测。

items.en: The adjective unexpectedly carries the negative prefix un- at its head.
items.cn: 形容词在词首带着否定前缀 un-。

items.en: -ly was added to the adjective, giving the adverb that marks how surprises happen.
items.cn: 形容词再加 -ly，得到标记意外发生的副词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the expect root, and the near-meaning group covers adverbs of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组收集 expect 词根的其他形式，近义组覆盖表示惊讶的副词。

entries.definition: not planned for
the quality of being a surprise
as was thought likely
in a very ordinary way
entries.definitionCN: 毫无例外地（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: quickly and without warning
in a way that causes surprise
in a short and rough way
as one could have guessed

normalIntro.en: The adverb is a judgement placed next to a verb, so it tells you how the surprise arrived.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词是贴在动词旁的评判，告诉你意外是怎么发生的。

normal.en: Un- plus expectedly: not as foreseen.
normal.cn: un- 加 expectedly：不像被预见的那样。

normal.en: Arrive unexpectedly is the pattern learners meet most often.
normal.cn: arrive unexpectedly 是学习者最常遇到的搭配。

normal.en: Before an adjective it marks surprising degree, as in unexpectedly high.
normal.cn: 放在形容词前时，它标记出人意料的程度，如 unexpectedly high。

normal.en: At the start of a clause it judges the whole sentence that follows.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，它评判后面整句话。

normal.en: The adjective is unexpected; the ending -ly adds manner.
normal.cn: 形容词是 unexpected，词尾 -ly 加上的正是「方式」。

abstract.en: Picture a doorbell ringing hours before you expect it.
abstract.cn: 想象门铃比预想的时间早了几个小时响起。

abstract.en: See a lift doors open on the wrong floor.
abstract.cn: 看电梯门在错的楼层打开。

abstract.en: Hear a voice say a name you had not spoken for years.
abstract.cn: 听一个声音说出你多年没叫过的名字。

examples.en: The old bridge collapsed unexpectedly on a dry, quiet night.
examples.cn: 那座旧桥在一个干燥安静的夜里意外坍塌。

examples.en: Unexpectedly, the shop had exactly the book she wanted.
examples.cn: 出乎意料的是，店里正好有她想要的那本书。

examples.en: Prices rose unexpectedly fast in the spring.
examples.cn: 春天物价出人意料地上涨得很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺尼可斯派克替德利」——俺还没说请，人就替德利先到了，真是意外得很。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ expectedly，expect 源自拉丁语 exspectare（向外张望），词根 spectare 意为「看」

sensesIntro.en: One adverb of surprise works beside verbs, before adjectives, and at the head of a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示意外的副词，既能贴动词、又能修饰形容词，还能站到句首。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone arriving before they were expected.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没到预期就出现的人。

branches.en: The event branch: what happens without planning or warning.
branches.cn: 事件分支：没有计划也没有预告发生的事。

branches.en: The degree branch: a level nobody guessed.
branches.cn: 程度分支：没人猜到的程度。

branches.en: The behaviour branch: people acting against expectation.
branches.cn: 行为分支：举动违背预期的那些人。

branches.en: The comment branch: a word that opens the sentence and judges it.
branches.cn: 评注分支：放在句首评论整句的词。

branches.en: The plain event sense that most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 学习者最先遇到的最朴素的「意外事件」义。

intro.en: Four small pieces, all visible: un-, the verb expect, the participle ending, and -ly.
intro.cn: 四个小部件全都看得见：un-、动词 expect、分词词尾与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The looking root spectare also survives in spectator and inspect.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「看」的词根 spectare 也存在于 spectator 与 inspect 中。

definition_zh: 纪念碑；纪念物；古迹；有永久价值的成就或证据
definition_en: a structure built to commemorate a person or event; a historic site; a lasting example or achievement
core_image: 广场中央的石柱在夕阳下投出长影，碑座上刻着几行名字
scene: 广场中央的石柱在夕阳下投出长影。 The monument honors the engineers who built the first bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 monument 指「为纪念人物或事件而建的纪念性建筑」（第 1 个义项：纪念建筑）；句意为这座纪念碑向建造第一座桥的工程师致敬；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 纪念碑；纪念物；古迹；典范；不朽成就

collocations.zh: 国家纪念碑；国家保护区

derivatives.zh: monument + -al（形容词后缀）→ 纪念碑的；巨大的
monumental + -ity（性质后缀）→ 纪念性；宏伟感
monumental + -ly（副词后缀）→ 巨大地；极其
monumental + -ize（动词后缀）→ 使成为纪念物

senses.title: A commemorative structure
senses.definition: a building, statue or stone erected to keep the memory of a person or event
senses.definitionCN: 为保存对某人或某事的记忆而建成的建筑、雕像或石碑
senses.example: The monument honors the engineers who built the first bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这座纪念碑向建造第一座桥的工程师致敬。
senses.why: monumentum came from monere 'to remind'; the structure exists to make people remember.
senses.whyCN: monumentum 来自 monere「提醒」；这座建筑存在的目的就是让人记住。

senses.title: A historic building or site
senses.definition: an old building, ruin or place preserved because of its historical importance
senses.definitionCN: 因历史重要性而被保存的古老建筑、废墟或地点
senses.example: The abbey is listed as a monument of national importance.
senses.exampleCN: 这座修道院被列为具有国家重要性的历史建筑。
senses.why: the same word moved from a purpose-built memorial to any old structure that a nation decides to protect.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从专门建造的纪念物，扩展到国家决定保护的任何古老建筑。

senses.title: A tombstone or grave memorial
senses.definition: a stone or structure marking a grave and preserving a name
senses.definitionCN: 标记墓地并保存姓名的石碑或建筑
senses.example: A simple monument marks the grave of the village teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 一块朴素的墓碑标出乡村教师的墓。
senses.why: a grave marker is the smallest and oldest kind of memorial, a stone that keeps one name in place.
senses.whyCN: 墓碑是最小、最古老的纪念物，一块石头把一个人的名字留在原处。

senses.title: A lasting evidence or example
senses.definition: something that stands as clear evidence of a quality, often a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 作为某种品质（常为负面）的明显证据的事物
senses.example: The empty factory is a monument to poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 那座空工厂是规划不善的活证据。
senses.why: the commemorative sense turns ironic: a thing can remind people of a failure as well as a hero.
senses.whyCN: 纪念义可转为反讽：事物既能让人记住英雄，也能让人记住失败。

senses.title: An outstanding achievement or work
senses.definition: a work or achievement so important that it deserves to be remembered
senses.definitionCN: 重要到值得被记住的作品或成就
senses.example: The dictionary is a monument of nineteenth-century scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 这部词典是十九世纪学术的不朽丰碑。
senses.why: what deserves a monument is what a culture wants to keep, so the word extends from stone to achievement.
senses.whyCN: 值得立碑的东西就是文化想留住的东西，因此词义从石头扩展到成就。

senses.title: An ancient ruin
senses.definition: a surviving structure of an earlier civilization, often visited as a heritage site
senses.definitionCN: 早期文明留存下来的建筑，常作为文化遗产参观
senses.example: Tourists walked among the monuments of the old capital.
senses.exampleCN: 游客在旧都的遗迹间行走。
senses.why: once a whole city is old enough, its surviving structures become monuments by age rather than by design.
senses.whyCN: 当整座城市足够古老，留存下来的建筑就凭年代而非设计成为遗迹。

senses.title: A statue
senses.definition: a sculpted figure set up in public to honor a person
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念某人而置于公共空间的雕塑人像
senses.example: A bronze monument of the founder stands in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 广场上立着创始人的铜像。
senses.why: a statue is a monument given a human shape, the memorial impulse turned into a sculpted body.
senses.whyCN: 雕像是一座拥有人形的纪念碑，是纪念冲动变成雕塑身体。

senses.title: A written memorial record
senses.definition: a written account or record kept to preserve someone's memory
senses.definitionCN: 为保存某人记忆而留下的书面记述或记录
senses.example: The chronicle is a monument in words rather than in stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这部编年史是用文字而非石头筑成的纪念碑。
senses.why: a written record performs the same reminding job as a stone, so the word extends to books and chronicles.
senses.whyCN: 书面记录承担与石头相同的提醒功能，因此词义扩展到书籍与编年史。

intro.en: Monument comes from Latin monumentum, 'a memorial, a monument', from monere 'to remind, warn'. The same verb gives monitor and admonish, so the core idea is something that makes you remember.
intro.cn: monument 来自拉丁 monumentum「纪念物、纪念碑」，源于 monere「提醒、警告」。同一动词还衍生 monitor 与 admonish，核心意思是「让人想起的东西」。

items.en: Monere meant 'to remind, warn, advise', the act behind every monument.
items.cn: monere 意为「提醒、警告、劝告」，是每座纪念碑背后的动作。

items.en: Monumentum was 'a thing that reminds', whether a building, a tomb or a written record.
items.cn: monumentum 指「使人想起的东西」，可以是建筑、坟墓或书面记录。

items.en: English borrowed the word first for a memorial structure or tomb.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，最初指纪念建筑或坟墓。

items.en: Later it covered preserved old buildings and ruins, especially in heritage law.
items.cn: 后来它覆盖受保护的古老建筑与废墟，尤其在遗产法规中。

items.en: The word then extended to achievements and to ironic examples, as in a monument to folly.
items.cn: 再后来扩展到成就与反讽例证，如「愚蠢的纪念碑」。

note.en: Group one holds memorial objects easily confused with a monument; group two holds words for importance and remembrance.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 monument 混淆的纪念物；第二组是表示重要与纪念的词。

entries.definition: A object or event that keeps a memory; a monument is one kind, usually built and public.
entries.definitionCN: 保存记忆的物件或活动；monument 是其中一种，通常是建成且公开的。

entries.definition: A small object kept as a reminder; it is personal, while a monument is public and large.
entries.definitionCN: 留作提醒的小物件；属私人性质，纪念碑则公开且宏大。

entries.definition: The describing word for a monument or for something huge; the noun is the object itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述纪念碑或巨大事物的形容词；名词指物件本身。

entries.definition: A written reminder or note; it shares the reminder root but names a document, not a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 书面提醒或便条；共享「提醒」词根，但指文件而非建筑。

entries.definition: A carved or cast figure of a person or animal; a monument may be a statue, but may also be a wall or arch.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物的雕刻或铸造形象；纪念碑可以是雕像，也可能是墙或拱门。

entries.definition: A holy place or structure marking a sacred person or event; the emphasis is religious.
entries.definitionCN: 标记神圣人物或事件的圣地或建筑；侧重宗教。

entries.definition: A easily recognized feature of a place; a monument is built to remember, a landmark may simply be noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方易被认出的特征；纪念碑为记忆而建，地标只是显眼。

entries.definition: A grave or burial chamber; a monument may mark a tomb but need not contain a body.
entries.definitionCN: 坟墓或墓室；纪念碑可标记坟墓，但不一定葬有遗体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin reminder verb, the real public object and the ironic extension.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「提醒」动词、真实的公共物件与反讽引申。

normal.en: monere is 'to remind'; a monument is a reminder made of stone.
normal.cn: monere 是「提醒」；纪念碑是用石头做成的提醒。

normal.en: Monitor and admonish come from the same verb.
normal.cn: monitor 与 admonish 同出这个动词。

normal.en: Heritage law uses monument for protected old buildings.
normal.cn: 遗产法规用 monument 指受保护的古老建筑。

normal.en: A monument can be ironic: a monument to bad planning.
normal.cn: 纪念碑可以带反讽：规划不善的纪念碑。

normal.en: A written chronicle can be called a monument in words.
normal.cn: 一部编年史可称为文字筑成的纪念碑。

abstract.en: A monument is a stone that keeps saying a name after the mouth is gone.
abstract.cn: 纪念碑是一块在嘴消失后仍不断念出名字的石头。

abstract.en: It is memory given a body heavy enough to stay put.
abstract.cn: 它是被赋予足够沉重身体、无法轻易移走的记忆。

abstract.en: A bad monument is a culture arguing with its own past.
abstract.cn: 糟糕的纪念碑，是一个文化在与自己的过去争吵。

examples.en: The city erected a monument to the nurses who died in the epidemic.
examples.cn: 这座城市为死于疫病的护士建立了纪念碑。

examples.en: The old bridge is a monument of early engineering.
examples.cn: 这座旧桥是早期工程的不朽之作。

examples.en: The empty tower stands as a monument to failed ambition.
examples.cn: 那座空塔成了野心失败的一座纪念碑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「monu（提醒）+ ment（物）」——让人记住的东西 → 纪念碑

root: 拉丁 monumentum「使人想起的东西」← monere「提醒、警告」+ -mentum（名词后缀）；同源词有 monitor、admonish。英语 monument。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one reminder: a built memorial, a protected site, a grave, a warning example, an achievement, a ruin, a statue and a written record.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个提醒展开：建成的纪念物、受保护遗址、坟墓、警示例证、成就、废墟、雕像与书面记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy stone standing in a square, repeating a name to everyone who passes.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上一块沉重的石头，向每个经过的人重复一个名字。

branches.en: STONE MEMORY: a public memorial and a grave marker both make a name outlast a life.
branches.cn: 石头记忆：公共纪念碑与墓碑都让名字活得比生命更久。

branches.en: PROTECTED PAST: a listed building and an ancient ruin are the past kept in place.
branches.cn: 受保护的过去：登录建筑与古代废墟都是被留在原地的过去。

branches.en: VALUE JUDGEMENT: an ironic example and a great achievement both measure a culture's memory.
branches.cn: 价值判断：反讽例证与伟大成就都在衡量一个文化的记忆。

branches.en: HUMAN FIGURE: a statue makes the reminder take a body.
branches.cn: 人形：雕像让提醒拥有身体。

branches.en: WRITTEN STONE: a chronicle is a monument made of words instead of rock.
branches.cn: 文字之石：编年史是用文字而非岩石筑成的纪念碑。

intro.en: Monument is a Latin reminder noun, and its family still carries the idea of warning and memory.
intro.cn: monument 是一个拉丁「提醒」名词，其词族仍带着警告与记忆的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin monere gives monitor, admonish and monumentum; the suffix -mentum turns the act of reminding into a thing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 monere 衍生 monitor、admonish 与 monumentum；后缀 -mentum 把「提醒」的动作变成物件。

items.structure: monere, monui, monitum (Latin verb, second conjugation)
items.example: The verb is the root of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的词根。

items.meaning: means or result of an action
items.example: The suffix turns reminding into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「提醒」变成物件。

items.example: The monument stands in the square.
The hall has a cold monumentality.
items.exampleCN: 大厅有一种冷峻的宏伟感。

definition_zh: 枕头；抱枕；靠垫；枕状垫块
definition_en: a soft cushion that supports the head in bed, and by extension any cushion one leans on or a pad placed under part of the body
core_image: 一只被压出浅浅头形的白枕头，枕套边上还留着折痕
scene: 雨夜的卧铺车厢里，窗帘半掩，铺位上摊着一条薄被。 She punched the pillow twice and turned to face the window.
sceneCN: 这里的 pillow 是「枕头」（第 1 个义项：睡觉时垫头的软垫）；句意是她把枕头拍了两下，转身面向车窗。图中可辨识物件：窗帘、薄被、铺位。

collocations.phrase: rest one's head on a pillow

derivatives.zh: 由 pillow 与 case 复合而成，义为「枕套」
由 pillow 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「枕状的；柔软的」

senses.title: A cushion for the head in bed
senses.definition: a soft bag filled with feathers, foam or grain, placed under the head while sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 装满羽毛、海绵或谷物的软袋，睡觉时垫在头下
senses.example: He fell asleep as soon as his head touched the pillow.
senses.exampleCN: 他的头一碰到枕头就睡着了。
senses.why: Old English pyle borrowed the Latin word for a cushion, and the first job of that cushion was to hold up a sleeping head.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pyle 借自拉丁语中表示「垫子」的词，而这种垫子最初的任务就是在睡梦中托住脑袋。

senses.title: A decorative cushion for leaning on
senses.definition: a smaller cushion kept on a sofa or chair so that sitting becomes more comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 放在沙发或椅子上、让坐姿更舒服的小垫子
senses.example: Three striped pillows were stacked at one end of the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 沙发一端叠着三个条纹靠垫。
senses.why: Once cushions moved from the bed to the living room, the old word travelled with them and now covers anything soft you lean against.
senses.whyCN: 垫子从床上搬到客厅之后，旧词也跟着搬了过去，如今泛指任何可以靠着的柔软之物。

senses.title: A pad that supports part of the body
senses.definition: a pad or block placed under a limb or a machine part to support it
senses.definitionCN: 垫在肢体或机器部件下方起承托作用的垫块
senses.example: The nurse slid a foam pillow under his injured ankle.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把一块泡沫垫塞到他受伤的脚踝下面。
senses.why: A pillow does one thing well, holding something up softly, so nursing and engineering borrowed the name for any pad that supports.
senses.whyCN: 枕头只把一件事做好，就是柔软地托住东西，于是护理和工程都借这个词来指任何起承托作用的垫子。

intro.en: Pillow is an Old English word for a cushion, and the cushion itself came from Latin; the exact route through the Germanic languages is not fully certain.
intro.cn: pillow 是古英语中表示垫子的词，而垫子这个概念来自拉丁语；它经由日耳曼诸语的具体路径并不完全确定。

items.en: Pulvinus named a cushion or bolster, and it could also mean the cushioned couch on which images of the gods were placed.
items.cn: pulvinus 指垫子、长靠枕，也可指安放神像的软榻。

items.en: Germanic speakers took the Latin cushion word over; the reconstructed form is usually written with an asterisk, and the exact route is described as uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语借用了拉丁语的「垫子」一词；重构形式通常带星号，具体路径一般认为并不确定。

items.en: Old English pyle meant both pillow and cushion, so the bed sense and the general sense started together.
items.cn: 古英语 pyle 同时指枕头和垫子，床上义与泛指义从一开始就并存。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word pilwe, with a w that later hardened into the modern ending.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 pilwe，词尾的 w 后来固定成现代形式。

items.en: Modern English settled on pillow and built compounds such as pillowcase and pillow talk on top of it.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 pillow，并在其上构成 pillowcase、pillow talk 等复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that only share letters or a syllable with pillow; the near-meaning group collects other soft supports.
note.cn: 形近组收只是与 pillow 共享字母或音节的词；近义组收其他柔软的承托物。

entries.definition: A small round dose of medicine; it only echoes the start of pillow, and the two have different Latin sources.
entries.definitionCN: 小圆药丸；只是与 pillow 开头相近，两者的拉丁来源不同。

entries.definition: A tree with long bending branches, often planted beside water.
entries.definitionCN: 枝条细长下垂、常种在水边的树。

entries.definition: To swell out like a sail filled with wind.
entries.definitionCN: 像灌满风的帆那样鼓起。

entries.definition: A tall upright post that holds up a building.
A soft pad used to sit on or lean against.
A long firm pillow, or to strengthen something.
entries.definitionCN: 长而结实的枕头；也指加强。

entries.definition: The part of a seat that supports the head.
entries.definitionCN: 座椅上支撑头部的部分。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the name of a cushion and never lost that softness; every later sense is a cushion doing its old job somewhere new.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「垫子」的名字开始，始终没丢掉那份柔软；后来每个义项都是垫子在新的地方做着旧工作。

normal.en: Pillow and Latin pulvinus both name a cushion, so softness is built into the word from the first record.
normal.cn: pillow 与拉丁语 pulvinus 都指垫子，柔软从最早的记录起就写进了这个词。

normal.en: Old English pyle already meant both pillow and cushion, which is why the bed sense and the sofa sense never fully split.
normal.cn: 古英语 pyle 本就兼指枕头和垫子，所以床上义与沙发义始终没有彻底分开。

normal.en: Pillowcase joins pillow to case, the ordinary English way of naming a cover for a thing.
normal.cn: pillowcase 把 pillow 与 case 组合起来，正是英语给某物的外套命名的常见办法。

normal.en: Pillow talk keeps the word in bed and turns it into a name for what is said there.
normal.cn: pillow talk 把词留在床上，用来指那里说出的私房话。

normal.en: Pillowy adds -y to say soft like a pillow, a suffix that turns a noun into a quality.
normal.cn: pillowy 加 -y 表示「像枕头一样软」，这个后缀把名词变成了性质。

abstract.en: A pillow is the one object whose whole purpose is to be forgotten while you sleep.
abstract.cn: 枕头是唯一一种整个用途就是让人睡着后忘掉它的东西。

abstract.en: Softness that holds you up is a useful picture for any support you stop noticing.
abstract.cn: 柔软的承托，是形容那些你不再察觉的支撑的好画面。

abstract.en: The word moved from bed to sofa to hospital without changing shape, only the place of rest.
abstract.cn: 这个词从床到沙发再到病房，形状没变，变的只是歇息的地方。

examples.en: He fell asleep as soon as his head touched the pillow.
examples.cn: 他的头一碰到枕头就睡着了。

examples.en: She bought two new pillow cases for the spare room.
examples.cn: 她给客房买了两只新枕套。

examples.en: The nurse slid a foam pillow under his injured ankle.
examples.cn: 护士把一块泡沫垫塞到他受伤的脚踝下面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮篓」——脑袋像装进一只软皮篓子，那就是枕头。

root: 古英语 pyle 经西日耳曼语借自拉丁语 pulvinus（垫子、靠枕），最初指睡觉时垫在头下的软垫。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the cushion under a sleeping head; the other senses carry the same soft support to the sofa and to the sickbed.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是睡梦中垫在头下的软垫；其余义项把同样的柔软承托带到沙发与病床。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white pillow with a shallow dent where a head has rested.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只白枕头被压出浅浅的头形凹痕。

branches.en: a head sinking into a soft bag at night
branches.cn: 夜里脑袋陷进软软的一袋填充物

branches.en: a hand fluffing the pillow before sleep
branches.cn: 睡前用手把枕头拍松

branches.en: three cushions stacked at one end of a sofa
branches.cn: 沙发一端叠着三个靠垫

branches.en: a foam pad slipped under an injured ankle
branches.cn: 垫在受伤脚踝下的泡沫垫

branches.en: soft support wherever the body rests
branches.cn: 身体歇着的地方都有柔软的承托

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin cushion noun, its Germanic and Old English descendants, and two English compounds that keep the softness in view.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语的「垫子」名词、它在日耳曼语和古英语中的后裔，以及两个保留柔软意象的英语复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin pulvinus is the cushion behind the English word, and its longer relative pulvinar names the cushioned couch of the gods.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pulvinus 是英语这个词背后的「垫子」，它更长的一个同族词 pulvinar 指安放神像的软榻。

definition_zh: 钦佩；赞赏；令人钦佩的对象
definition_en: a feeling of great respect and warm approval, or the person or thing that causes it
core_image: 人群抬头看着走钢丝的人抵达对面，忍不住鼓起掌来
scene: 演出结束，观众站起来鼓掌，久久不肯离场。 Her courage won the admiration of everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里的 admiration 是「钦佩」（第 1 个义项：由衷的敬意）；句意是她的勇气赢得了在场所有人的钦佩。

pos.zh: 名词：钦佩；赞赏；令人钦佩的人或物

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「钦佩；欣赏」
由动词加表人后缀构成，义为「钦佩者；爱慕者」
由动词词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「值得钦佩的」
由动词加分词后缀构成，义为「赞赏的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「令人钦佩地」

senses.title: A feeling of great respect
senses.definition: a feeling of respect mixed with warm approval for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物怀有的敬意，并带温暖的赞许
senses.example: She looked at the painting with admiration.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀着钦佩之情看着那幅画。
senses.why: Latin admirari joined ad- 'to' with mirari 'to wonder', so admiration is wonder turned towards something worth looking up to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 admirari 是 ad-（向）加 mirari（惊叹），所以 admiration 是「惊叹」转向某个值得仰望的对象。

senses.title: The person or thing admired
senses.definition: someone or something that is the object of widespread praise and wonder
senses.definitionCN: 广受赞美与惊叹的人或事物
senses.example: The young pianist was the admiration of the whole school.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻的钢琴手成了全校钦佩的对象。
senses.why: The feeling and its object exchange places easily: what everyone wonders at becomes, in the old phrase, the admiration of all.
senses.whyCN: 情感与对象很容易互换位置：众人惊叹之物，用旧说法就是「众人的 admiration」。

intro.en: Wonder, directed at something, becomes respect.
intro.cn: 惊叹一旦指向某个对象，就成了敬意。

items.en: mirari meant to wonder at or marvel, and gave mirror and miracle.
items.cn: mirari 意为惊叹、惊奇，也生出 mirror 与 miracle。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus mirari formed admirari, to wonder at, to regard with wonder.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 mirari 构成 admirari，意为「对……惊叹、以惊奇的目光看待」。

items.en: admiratio named the feeling of wonder and esteem.
items.cn: admiratio 指惊叹与敬意交织的情感。

items.en: Old French carried the noun into English with the sense of wondering esteem.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带入英语，义为「带着惊叹的敬重」。

items.en: The modern word is milder than wonder: it praises without losing distance.
items.cn: 现代词义比「惊叹」温和：它在赞美时仍保持一点距离。

note.en: The first group is the mirari family; the second gathers feelings of approval with different heat.
note.cn: 第一组是 mirari 词族；第二组收几种热度不同的赞许之情。

normalIntro.en: mirari, to wonder, is the heart of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 意为「惊叹」的 mirari，是这个词的心脏。

normal.en: admire plus -ation gives the feeling; admire plus -er gives the person who feels it.
normal.cn: admire 加 -ation 是情感，加 -er 是怀有情感的人。

normal.en: The usual pattern is admiration for someone or something.
normal.cn: 常用搭配是 admiration for（对……的钦佩）。

normal.en: in admiration describes the way someone looks or speaks.
normal.cn: in admiration 描述一个人看或说的神态。

normal.en: admiration is uncountable in the feeling sense.
normal.cn: 表示「情感」时，admiration 不可数。

normal.en: Keep the -ation ending; do not write admirment.
normal.cn: 词尾是 -ation，不要写成 admirment。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd looking up at a tightrope walker.
abstract.cn: 想象人群仰头看着走钢丝的人。

abstract.en: See a child holding a drawing up to the light.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子把一幅画举到光下细看。

abstract.en: Think of applause that goes on a little too long.
abstract.cn: 想象掌声持续得稍微久了些。

examples.en: She looked at the painting with admiration.
examples.cn: 她怀着钦佩之情看着那幅画。

examples.en: His honesty earned him wide admiration.
examples.cn: 他的诚实为他赢得了广泛的钦佩。

examples.en: The young pianist was the admiration of the whole school.
examples.cn: 这位年轻的钢琴手成了全校钦佩的对象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的米雷申」——额头上写着米雷申的名字，因为全场都在为他的表演鼓掌。

root: 拉丁语 admiratio（惊叹、敬意），出自 admirari（对……惊叹），由 ad-（向）与 mirari（惊奇）构成；本义「惊叹地注视」，后指钦佩。

sensesIntro.en: Wonder aimed at a person becomes respect, and sometimes the person himself.
sensesIntro.cn: 惊叹一旦对准某个人就成了敬意，有时还直接指那个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd looking up and applauding.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群仰头鼓掌。

branches.en: a viewer silent before a painting
branches.cn: 在画前沉默的观者

branches.en: students praising a teacher's patience
branches.cn: 学生称赞老师的耐心

branches.en: a pianist everyone talks about
branches.cn: 人人谈论的钢琴手

branches.en: a bridge engineers come to see
branches.cn: 工程师专程来看的桥

branches.en: the feeling and the thing that causes it
branches.cn: 情感与引起它的对象

intro.cn: 一个方向词头、一个表示惊叹的词根、一个名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: mirari also gives miracle, mirror and marvel.
latinIntro.cn: mirari 也给出 miracle、mirror 与 marvel。

definition_zh: 无论在哪里；在任何地方；四处
definition_en: in or to any place at all, or in every place that, used when the location does not need to be named
core_image: 一张没有边界的地图上，每个角落都插着一面小旗
scene: 她把地图铺开，随手在各个角落都插上小旗，说随便哪一面都行。 Wherever you sit, you will hear the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 wherever 是「无论在哪里」（第 1 个义项：任何地点都可以）；句意为你坐在哪里，都能听见海声。地图每个角落都插着小旗，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 无论在哪里；凡是…的地方

senses.title: In any place at all
senses.titleCN: 无论在哪里；不管什么地方
senses.definition: used to say that every possible place is included
senses.definitionCN: 表示一切可能的地点都包括在内
senses.example: Wherever you sit, you will hear the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 你坐在哪里，都能听见海声。
senses.why: The suffix -ever turns where from a question into a total, exactly as it does for when and what.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ever 把 where 从问句变成全称，与处理 when、what 的方式完全相同。

senses.title: In every place that
senses.definition: used with a verb of scattered covering to mean in all the places concerned
senses.definitionCN: 与散布、覆盖类动词连用，指所涉及的每一处
senses.example: Wherever they went, the reporters followed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们走到哪里，记者就跟到哪里。
senses.why: Covering all places means covering each place as it appears, so the word also marks repeated places.
senses.whyCN: 包揽所有地点也就是逐一覆盖每一处，于是这个词也标记重复出现的地点。

senses.title: Said alone, meaning any place suits
senses.definition: used as a short answer to say that no particular place is preferred
senses.definitionCN: 作简短回答，表示不偏好任何具体地点
senses.example: Wherever. The town is small and we can walk.
senses.exampleCN: 哪儿都行，小镇不大，走过去就好。
senses.why: One word takes the place of a whole list of possible sites, and so becomes an answer on its own.
senses.whyCN: 一个词替代一长串可能的地点，于是自成回答。

intro.en: Wherever is a Middle English compound of where and ever, made on the pattern of whatever and whichever.
intro.cn: wherever 是中古英语里 where 与 ever 的复合词，仿照 whatever、whichever 的模式构成。

items.en: Hwær and æfre were separate words, meaning where and ever.
items.cn: hwær 与 æfre 是两个分开的词，意为「何处」与「永远」。

items.en: The two were joined into wherever, which took over the older phrase in all places that.
items.cn: 两者连成 wherever，接管了旧说法「在所有的地方」。

items.en: The word spread through travel writing, where it marked any destination without naming it.
items.cn: 这个词在游记中传播，用来标记任何未点名的目的地。

items.en: Set phrases such as wherever possible made it common in official instructions.
items.cn: wherever possible 等固定短语让它在官方说明中变得常见。

items.en: In speech it also stands alone as a casual answer meaning any place is fine.
items.cn: 在口语中它还能单独作为随意回答，表示哪儿都行。

note.en: The first group gathers the -ever family and the opposite pairs, the second the words for any place and for everywhere.
note.cn: 第一组收 -ever 词族与成对的相反方向词，第二组收表示任何地方与到处说法。

entries.definition: The plain question word without the total sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不带全称意味的普通疑问词

entries.definition: The time version of the same compound.
A contrast word that shares the first half.
The heavy, old form of wherever.
In all places, stated rather than left open.
In any place, the plain phrase behind the compound.
In one unspecified place, narrower than wherever.

normalIntro.en: The word is where with ever on the end, so every point on the map is lit at once.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 where 加上结尾的 ever，于是地图上每一点同时亮起。

normal.en: Where stays in the question; wherever closes the question by covering all places.
normal.cn: where 留在问句里，wherever 用覆盖所有地点来关掉问句。

normal.en: The -ever trick works on every wh word: wherever, whenever, whoever, whatever.
normal.cn: -ever 这招对每个 wh 词都有效：wherever、whenever、whoever、whatever。

normal.en: Everywhere states the total; wherever leaves the door open.
normal.cn: everywhere 陈述全部，wherever 把门留着。

normal.en: Wherever possible is the commonest formal pairing.
normal.cn: wherever possible 是最常见的正式搭配。

normal.en: Said alone with a shrug, it means the place does not matter.
normal.cn: 耸着肩单独说出来，意思是地点无关紧要。

abstract.en: See flags planted in every corner of a map.
abstract.cn: 看地图每个角落都插上了旗。

abstract.en: Hear the same sea from every window.
abstract.cn: 从每一扇窗听到同一片海。

abstract.en: Feel a crowd follow someone from street to street.
abstract.cn: 感觉一群人从一条街跟到另一条街。

examples.en: Wherever she travels, she sends a postcard home.
examples.cn: 她无论去哪儿旅行，都会寄一张明信片回家。

examples.en: You can leave your bag wherever you like.
examples.cn: 你把包放哪儿都行。

examples.en: Wherever possible, the team works from home.
examples.cn: 只要有可能，团队就在家工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔艾佛」——威尔和艾佛说：人到哪儿，旗就插到哪儿。

root: 中古英语 where + ever 复合；同族有 wheresoever、whenever、whatever。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers every place, then spreads over each repeated place, and finally stands alone as a casual answer.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先包揽每一个地点，再铺到每一处重复出现的地方，最后单独站成随意的回答。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small flags in every corner of a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图每个角落都插着小旗。

branches.en: The open branch: wherever you sit, you hear the sea.
branches.cn: 开放分支：坐哪儿都能听见海。

branches.en: The spread branch: wherever they went, the reporters followed.
branches.cn: 分布分支：他们走到哪里记者就跟到哪里。

branches.en: The answer branch: wherever, the town is small.
branches.cn: 回答分支：哪儿都行，小镇不大。

branches.en: The formal branch: wherever possible in written rules.
branches.cn: 正式分支：书面规定中的 wherever possible。

branches.en: The family branch: wheresoever and whenever on the same plan.
branches.cn: 词族分支：wheresoever 与 whenever 同构。

intro.en: Wherever is where plus -ever, and the heavier -soever version still exists for legal and religious uses.
intro.cn: wherever 是 where 加 -ever，更重的 -soever 形式仍存在于法律与宗教文字中。

latinIntro.en: Latin used ubicumque for wherever, joining its place word with a generalising suffix; the entries below are the parallel forms, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 ubicumque 表「无论何处」，把地点词与概括性词尾结合起来；下面条目是并行形式，不是祖源。

senses.title: A prison
senses.definition: a building where people are kept as punishment for crimes
senses.definitionCN: 关押罪犯作为惩罚的建筑物
senses.example: The thief was sent to gaol.

senses.title: To imprison

senses.example: He was gaoled for two years.

definition_zh: 属性，特质；把……归因于；认为（作品）出自……
definition_en: a quality that belongs to a person or thing, or to say that something is caused by or made by someone
core_image: 一件物品上系着标签，写着它是什么、从哪里来
scene: 老师在评语里写下这个学生最突出的特点。 Patience is the attribute every good teacher needs.
sceneCN: 这里 attribute 是「特质、属性」（第 1 个义项）；句意是耐心是每位好老师都需要的特质。

pos.zh: 动词：把……归因于；认为出自

senses.title: Mark of a thing
senses.definition: a quality or feature that belongs to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 属于某人或某物的性质或特征
senses.example: Kindness was his most striking attribute.
senses.exampleCN: 善良是他最突出的特质。
senses.why: The noun keeps the old sense of something allotted to a thing: an attribute is a quality assigned to whatever carries it.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「分派给某物」的旧义：属性就是分配给承载者的那种性质。

senses.title: Name the cause
senses.definition: to say that something is the result of a particular cause
senses.definitionCN: 认为某结果是某个原因造成的
senses.example: She attributes her success to hard work.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己的成功归功于努力。
senses.why: The verb reverses the direction: instead of giving a quality to a thing, you give an effect back to the cause that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把方向倒过来：不是把性质给某物，而是把一个结果送回造成它的原因。

senses.title: Name the maker
senses.definition: to believe that a work was produced by a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 认为某件作品是由某个特定的人创作的
senses.example: The painting was attributed to an unknown artist.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画被认定出自一位不知名的画家之手。
senses.why: Authorship is treated as another kind of allotment: the work is assigned back to the hand that made it.
senses.whyCN: 作者身份被视为另一种「分派」：把作品重新分配给做出它的那只手。

intro.en: Attribute began as a legal word for something allotted to a person.
intro.cn: attribute 最初是个法律用语，指分派给某人的东西。

items.en: tribuere meant 'to allot or assign'.
items.cn: tribuere 意为「分配、分派」。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus tribuere made attribuere, 'to assign to'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 tribuere 构成 attribuere，意为「分派给」。

items.en: attributum was the thing assigned or credited.
items.cn: attributum 指被分派或归到某人名下的东西。

items.en: French attribut named a quality belonging to something.
items.cn: 法语 attribut 指属于某物的性质。

items.en: English split the word into a noun of quality and a verb of assigning causes.
items.cn: 英语把它分成表示性质的名词与表示归因的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tribute root; the near-meaning group gives nouns of quality and verbs of explaining causes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tribute 词根；近义组是表示性质的名词与解释原因的动词。

normalIntro.en: As a noun it names a quality; as a verb it hands an effect back to its cause.
normalIntro.cn: 作名词时它指一种性质；作动词时它把结果交还给原因。

normal.en: The noun stresses the first syllable, the verb the second.
normal.cn: 作名词时重音在第一音节，作动词时重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Attribute to is the verb pattern: attribute success to luck.
normal.cn: 动词搭配是 attribute to，例如把成功归因于运气。

normal.en: An attribute is something a person or thing simply has.
normal.cn: attribute 作名词时，就是人或物本身具有的某种特质。

normal.en: To attribute a painting to an artist is to name its maker.
normal.cn: 把画作归到某位画家名下，就是认定它的作者。

normal.en: The root tribute means to give or allot.
normal.cn: 词根 tribute 意为「给予、分配」。

abstract.en: See a label tied to an object, naming what it is.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签系在物品上，写明它是什么。

abstract.en: See a line drawn from an effect back to its cause.
abstract.cn: 想象一条线从结果往回连到原因。

abstract.en: See a signature appear under a painting that had none.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅原本无款的画作下方浮现出签名。

examples.en: Kindness was his most striking attribute.
examples.cn: 善良是他最突出的特质。

examples.en: The painting was attributed to an unknown artist.

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tribute（分配）：分给某物的性质就是属性；把结果分回给某个原因，就是归因。

root: 源自拉丁语 attribuere「分派给」，由 ad-「向」与 tribuere「分配」构成，名词形式 attributum；经法语 attribut 进入英语，由「分派之物」引申为属性，又引申为把结果归到某个原因或作者名下。

sensesIntro.en: The same act of allotting produces both a quality and an explanation.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「分配」的动作，既产生了一种性质，也产生了一种解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label tied to a thing, naming its owner and nature.

branches.cn: 认定画作出自某画家

definition_zh: 致命的；毁灭性的；命中注定的
definition_en: causing death, causing failure or ruin, or in older use fixed by fate
core_image: 雨夜的山路上，失控的汽车冲向护栏，警示灯闪个不停
scene: 超速导致了一场致命的事故。 Speeding caused a fatal accident.
sceneCN: 这里 fatal 是「致命的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：超速导致了一场致命的事故。

senses.title: Causing death
senses.definition: causing death or serious harm
senses.definitionCN: 造成死亡或严重伤害的
senses.example: Speeding caused a fatal accident.
senses.exampleCN: 超速导致了一场致命的事故。
senses.why: The main modern sense is deadly consequence.
senses.whyCN: 主要现代义是致命后果。

senses.title: Causing ruin
senses.definition: causing failure or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 造成失败或灾难的
senses.example: One fatal mistake ruined the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 一个致命的错误毁了整个计划。
senses.why: The sense extends from death to total ruin.
senses.whyCN: 词义从死亡延伸到彻底毁灭。

senses.title: Fixed by fate
senses.definition: decided by fate, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 在较古老或文学用法中由命运决定的
senses.example: In the old tale, a fatal prophecy came true.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老的故事里，一个命中注定的预言应验了。
senses.why: The original sense came from the idea of fate.
senses.whyCN: 最初的义项来自命运观念。

intro.en: Fatal comes from Latin fatalis, fixed by fate, from fatum, fate.
intro.cn: fatal 源自拉丁语 fatalis（由命运决定的），来自 fatum（命运）。

items.en: Fatum meant a spoken decree or fate.
items.cn: fatum 意为说出的话、神谕或命运。

items.en: Fatalis meant fixed by fate.
items.cn: fatalis 意为由命运决定的。

items.en: Fatal meant appointed by destiny.
items.cn: fatal 意为命中注定的。

items.en: Fatal came to mean causing death or ruin.
items.cn: fatal 开始表示造成死亡或毁灭的。

items.en: Fatal now mainly means deadly or disastrous.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fatal 主要表示致命的或灾难性的。

note.en: Fatal is compared with similar forms and with adjectives for deadly harm.
note.cn: 把 fatal 与形近词以及表示致命伤害的形容词作比较。

entries.definition: having important consequences
coming at the end
relating to an unborn baby
able to cause death
causing death, often by design
causing death, or subject to death

normalIntro.en: Fatal is fate plus the adjective ending al.
normalIntro.cn: fatal 是 fate 加形容词结尾 al。

normal.en: Fatal contains fate plus al.
normal.cn: fatal 由 fate 加 al 构成。

normal.en: A fatal accident causes death.
normal.cn: 致命事故会造成死亡。

normal.en: A fatal mistake can ruin a plan.
normal.cn: 致命错误会毁掉计划。

normal.en: Fatally means in a deadly way.
normal.cn: fatally 意为致命地。

normal.en: Fatal and fateful are related but not the same.
normal.cn: fatal 与 fateful 相关但含义不同。

abstract.en: Fatal moves from destiny to death.
abstract.cn: fatal 从命运义走向死亡义。

abstract.en: What fate decides becomes what cannot be avoided.
abstract.cn: 命运决定的事变成无法避免的事。

abstract.en: A fatal flaw is one that ends the story.
abstract.cn: 致命缺陷就是会终结故事的缺陷。

examples.en: The illness proved fatal within a week.
examples.cn: 这种病在一周内就夺去了生命。

examples.en: A fatal flaw sank the project.
examples.cn: 一个致命缺陷让项目失败了。

examples.en: They made the fatal error of trusting him.
examples.cn: 他们犯了信任他的致命错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: fate 是「命运」，fatal 原义「由命运决定的」，后来主要指「致命的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 fatalis（由命运决定的），来自 fatum（命运）。

sensesIntro.en: Fatal means causing death, causing ruin, or in older use fixed by fate.
sensesIntro.cn: fatal 意为致命的、造成毁灭的，或在旧用法中命中注定的。

core.en: An outcome that ends life or a plan.
core.cn: 终结生命或计划的结局。

branches.en: Something that causes death.
branches.cn: 造成死亡的事物。

branches.en: Something that destroys a plan or hope.
branches.cn: 摧毁计划或希望的事物。

branches.en: Something decided by destiny.
branches.cn: 由命运决定的事物。

branches.en: Death and ruin both mark an ending.
branches.cn: 死亡与毁灭都标记着终结。

branches.en: Destiny and death were once closely linked.
branches.cn: 命运与死亡曾经紧密相连。

intro.en: Fatal forms adverbs, nouns, and words about destiny.
intro.cn: fatal 构成副词、名词以及表示命运的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin fatum, fate, is the direct source.

items.meaning: a death caused by accident or violence
items.exampleCN: 这场撞车造成一人死亡。

items.example: Fatalities fell after the new rules.
items.exampleCN: 新规实施后死亡人数下降。

items.meaning: the belief that events are fixed
items.example: Fatalism can stop people from trying.
items.exampleCN: 宿命论会让人放弃尝试。

items.meaning: a person who believes in fate
items.example: The fatalist accepted the news calmly.
items.exampleCN: 宿命论者平静地接受了消息。

items.example: He has a fatalistic view of life.
items.exampleCN: 他对人生持宿命论观点。

items.example: The road was closed after a fatal accident.

definition_zh: 机密的；保密的；表示信任的
definition_en: meant to be kept secret and not shared with other people
core_image: 一份文件封口处盖着红色的保密印章
scene: 秘书把标着保密的档案锁进柜子。 Only a few staff may read this confidential file.
sceneCN: 这里 confidential 指「机密的」（第 1 个义项：只允许少数人知道）；句意是只有少数员工可以阅读这份机密文件。

pos.zh: 机密的；保密的；表示信任的

senses.title: Meant to be kept secret
senses.definition: described as information that only a few people may know
senses.definitionCN: 指只允许少数人知道的信息
senses.example: The report is confidential until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告在周五之前都是保密的。
senses.why: A secret shared too widely stops being a secret at all.
senses.whyCN: 秘密一旦传得太广，就不再是秘密。

senses.title: Showing private trust
senses.definition: used about a voice or manner that suggests a shared secret
senses.definitionCN: 形容语气或态度暗示着彼此共享秘密
senses.example: She spoke in a confidential tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一种表示信任的语气说话。
senses.why: A lowered voice signals that the words are meant only for you.
senses.whyCN: 压低的声音表示这些话只说给你听。

intro.en: Confidential comes from Latin confidentia, trust, and first described something said to a trusted person.
intro.cn: confidential 来自拉丁语 confidentia（信任），最初描述只对可信之人说的事。

items.en: Fidere meant to trust, and confidere meant to trust fully.
items.cn: fidere 意为信任，confidere 意为完全信任。

items.en: Confidentia named the bond of trust between people.
items.cn: confidentia 指人与人之间的信任纽带。

items.en: English confidential first described a person who could be trusted.
items.cn: 英语 confidential 最初描述值得信任的人。

items.en: It shifted to papers and words that must stay secret.
items.cn: 后来它转向指必须保密的文件与话语。

items.en: It now labels secret documents and also a quietly trusting manner.
items.cn: 如今它标注机密文件，也形容一种低声而信任的态度。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words from the same trust family, and the meaning group names other words for what is not public.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一信任词族的词，近义组列出其他表示不公开的说法。

entries.definition: sure about one's own ability

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a sealed folder, then move to a locked drawer and to a voice lowered to a whisper.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从封好的文件夹开始，再走到上锁的抽屉与压低成耳语的声音。

normal.en: Confidence plus -ial describes something that must stay inside a trusted circle.
normal.cn: confidence 加 -ial，描述必须留在可信圈子里的东西。

normal.en: A confidential file is a file with a lock on its mouth.
normal.cn: 机密文件，就是嘴上上了锁的文件。

normal.en: Strictly confidential means even the title stays quiet.
normal.cn: 严格保密，意思是连标题都不能外传。

normal.en: A confidential tone pulls two chairs closer together.
normal.cn: 表示信任的语气，会把两把椅子拉得更近。

normal.en: If you must promise first, the news is confidential.
normal.cn: 若对方要先让你保证，那条消息就是机密的。

abstract.en: Picture two heads leaning across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象两个脑袋隔着桌子靠拢。

examples.en: Please keep this information strictly confidential.
examples.cn: 请对这条信息严格保密。

examples.en: The company lost a confidential document.
examples.cn: 公司丢了一份机密文件。

examples.en: He leaned closer and spoke in a confidential voice.
examples.cn: 他凑近一些，用表示信任的低声说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confidential 记成 confidence（信任）加 ial：只有在信任的人之间才能传的东西，就是机密的。

root: 源自拉丁语 confidentia（信任），本义是只对可信之人说的事，后引申为机密的与表示信任的。

sensesIntro.en: From a fact held inside a trusted circle, to the quiet voice that shares it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从留在可信圈子内的事实，到分享它时那种压低的声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed envelope, a locked drawer, and two people speaking softly.
core.cn: 核心意象：封好的信封、上锁的抽屉，以及两个低声说话的人。

branches.en: The document sense is the most common and the most formal.
branches.cn: 文件义项最常见，也最正式。

branches.en: The manner sense shows trust through the way words are said.
branches.cn: 态度义项通过说话的方式表现出信任。

branches.en: Both senses assume that only a few people are allowed in.
branches.cn: 两个义项都假定只有少数人被允许进入。

branches.en: A confidential paper is protected by rules, not by luck.
branches.cn: 机密文件靠制度保护，而不是靠运气。

branches.en: A confidential tone is the sound of a circle closing.
branches.cn: 表示信任的语气，是一个圈子收拢时发出的声音。

intro.en: Confidential is confidentia, trust, plus the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: confidential 由 confidentia（信任）与形容词词尾 -al 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin trust base fid- also appears in fidelity and confident.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的信任词基 fid- 也出现在 fidelity 与 confident 中。

items.meaning: kept secret among a few people
in a secret or private way
the duty of keeping information secret
items.exampleCN: 医生必须遵守保密义务。

items.example: She is confident of a good result.

items.meaning: to tell a secret in trust
items.example: He confided the truth to her.
Only her confidant knew the plan.
items.exampleCN: 只有她的知己知道这个计划。

items.example: The file is classified by the army.
items.exampleCN: 这份文件被军方列为机密。

definition_zh: 宿舍；宿舍楼；宿舍房间；宿舍的
definition_en: a student residence hall, a room inside it, or a word used before another noun for student housing
core_image: 熄灯后的走廊，一串钥匙轻轻碰在一起
scene: 熄灯后的走廊只剩脚步声，钥匙在锁孔里转了半圈。 She tiptoed back to the dorm after the library closed.
sceneCN: 这里 dorm 是「学生宿舍」（第 1 个义项：学生住的宿舍楼，dormitory 的口语简称）；句意是图书馆关门后她踮着脚回到了宿舍。

pos.zh: 名词：宿舍；宿舍楼；宿舍房间
形容词性用法：宿舍的（多用于复合词）

derivatives.zh: 本词的全称，义为「宿舍；集体宿舍」
由本词加 mate「同伴」构成，义为「宿舍室友」
由本词加 room 构成的复合词，义为「宿舍房间」

senses.title: A student residence hall
senses.definition: a building where students live during term time, the informal short form of dormitory
senses.definitionCN: 学期内学生居住的楼房，是 dormitory 的口语简称
senses.example: The dorm stands next to the sports field.
senses.exampleCN: 宿舍楼紧挨着运动场。
senses.why: Students cut the long Latin-derived dormitory down to four letters, but kept the building and its communal life in the short form.
senses.whyCN: 学生把源自拉丁语的长词 dormitory 缩成四个字母，但这一简称仍然保留了那栋楼和集体生活。

senses.title: A room in a hall
senses.definition: a single room used by a student inside a residence hall
senses.definitionCN: 宿舍楼里供一名学生使用的单个房间
senses.example: His dorm is small but has a desk by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他的宿舍不大，但窗边有一张书桌。
senses.why: The building name slides down to the room, since students speak of the place they actually sleep in.
senses.whyCN: 楼房的名称滑落到房间上，因为学生说的是自己真正睡觉的那个地方。

senses.title: Of student housing
senses.definition: used before another noun to describe things connected with student housing
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一个名词前，描述与学生住宿有关的事物
senses.example: Dorm food is cheap but rarely exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 宿舍饭菜便宜，但很少让人惊喜。
senses.why: A place name easily becomes a label, so dorm attaches to food, life and mates as if it were an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 地名很容易变成标签，于是 dorm 像形容词一样贴到 food、life 与 mate 前面。

intro.en: Dorm is a clipped form of dormitory, from Latin dormitorium, a sleeping place.
intro.cn: dorm 是 dormitory 的缩略形式，后者来自拉丁语 dormitorium（睡觉的地方）。

items.en: Dormire meant to sleep, and it sits at the base of the whole family.
items.cn: dormire 意为「睡觉」，是整个词族的基底。

items.en: Dormitorium named a sleeping room, especially one shared by several people.
items.cn: dormitorium 指睡觉的房间，尤指多人共用的房间。

items.en: English dormitory first named a shared sleeping room in a monastery or school.
items.cn: 英语 dormitory 最初指修道院或学校里共用的睡房。

items.en: Universities expanded dormitories into large residence buildings for students.
items.cn: 大学把 dormitory 扩展成大型学生宿舍楼。

items.en: The clipped form dorm spread in student speech and in campus notices.
items.cn: 缩略形式 dorm 在学生口语与校园告示中流行起来。

items.en: Dorm now appears in compounds such as dorm room and dorm life.
items.cn: 今天 dorm 出现在 dorm room、dorm life 这类复合词中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin sleep root; the near-meaning group names other shared housing.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「睡」的词根；近义组收的是其他集体住处。

entries.definition: The full word for a student residence or shared sleeping building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宿舍、集体宿舍」，是 dorm 的全称。

entries.definition: A window set in a roof, from an old word for a sleeping room.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「屋顶窗」，来自旧时表示睡房的词，与 dorm 同源。

entries.definition: A rare word meaning causing sleep.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「催眠的；安眠药」，较少使用，同出 dormire。

entries.definition: A formal American term for a student dormitory building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「学生宿舍楼」，是美式正式说法。

entries.definition: Cheap shared accommodation for travellers or students.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「旅舍、青年宿舍」，指廉价共住的住处。

entries.definition: A large building or room; at universities it can mean a residence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大厅、楼」，在大学语境里也可指宿舍楼。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real dormire family from a sleeping room to a campus building.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 dormire 词族，从一间睡房走到校园里的宿舍楼。

normal.en: Dormire is to sleep; dormitorium is the place for it.
normal.cn: dormire 是睡觉，dormitorium 就是睡觉的地方。

normal.en: Dormitory was first a shared sleeping room, then a whole building.
normal.cn: dormitory 先是共用的睡房，后来才指整栋楼。

normal.en: Dorm is just the first syllable that students kept.
normal.cn: dorm 只是学生保留下来的第一个音节。

normal.en: Dorm life and dorm food use the place name as a label.
normal.cn: dorm life 与 dorm food 把这个地名当作标签来用。

normal.en: A dormer window and a dorm share the same sleep root.
normal.cn: dormer window（屋顶窗）与 dorm 共享同一个「睡」词根。

abstract.en: Picture a dark corridor where one key turns in a lock.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗的走廊里，一把钥匙在锁孔里转动。

abstract.en: Picture four desks pushed against one wall of a small room.
abstract.cn: 想象四张书桌挤在一间小屋的同一面墙边。

abstract.en: Picture a whole building where every window goes dark at the same minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一整栋楼，每扇窗都在同一分钟暗下去。

examples.en: The dorm is quiet during the exam week.
examples.cn: 考试周期间宿舍很安静。

examples.en: She keeps a small plant on her dorm windowsill.
examples.cn: 她在宿舍窗台上养了一小盆植物。

examples.en: Dorm life taught him to share a kitchen.
examples.cn: 宿舍生活教会他与人共用厨房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逗梦」——宿舍是学生一起做梦、互相逗趣的地方，dorm 就是宿舍。

root: dorm 是 dormitory 的缩略形式。dormitory 源自拉丁语 dormitorium（睡觉的地方），由 dormire（睡）加表示地点的后缀 -torium 构成。英语十五世纪先以它指修道院或学校的共用睡房，十九世纪扩展为宿舍楼，二十世纪学生口语把它截成 dorm。

sensesIntro.en: One clipped word covers the building, the single room and the label attached to student life.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个缩略词，覆盖宿舍楼、单个房间，以及贴在学生生活上的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark corridor after lights out, with keys clicking softly.
core.cn: 核心意象：熄灯后的黑暗走廊，钥匙轻碰作响。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: the first sense is the residence hall as a whole.
branches.cn: 楼宇线：第一个义项是作为整体的宿舍楼。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the second sense narrows the building to one student's room.
branches.cn: 房间线：第二个义项把整栋楼缩小到一名学生的房间。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the third sense uses the place name before other nouns.
branches.cn: 标签线：第三个义项把这个地名放到别的名词前面。

branches.en: Building and room share the name because students move between the two every day.
branches.cn: 整栋楼与单个房间共用一个名字，因为学生每天都在两者之间来回。

branches.en: The room becomes a label: dorm food is food experienced in that room.
branches.cn: 房间变成标签：dorm food 就是在那间房里吃到的饭。

intro.en: Dorm is a clipped Latin-derived stem with a place suffix -torium behind it.
intro.cn: dorm 是截短了的拉丁词干，背后带着表示地点的后缀 -torium。

latinIntro.en: Latin dormire and dormitorium are recorded; the adjective dormitorius also existed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dormire 与 dormitorium 均有记录，形容词 dormitorius 也存在。

items.example: The verb is the sleep root.
The noun named a shared sleeping room.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指共用的睡房。

items.example: She lives in a dorm near the library.
items.exampleCN: 她住在图书馆附近的宿舍。

items.example: The two dorms face each other.

derivatives.zh: 本词的全称，义为「宿舍；集体宿舍」
由本词加 mate「同伴」构成，义为「宿舍室友」
由本词加 room 构成的复合词，义为「宿舍房间」

definition_zh: 向外的；朝外的；外表的；外部的；向外
definition_en: directed or moving away from the centre, concerning the outside rather than the inner nature, or in a direction away from something
core_image: 一件外套被翻过来，里子朝内，布面朝外，风从那一面吹过去
scene: 码头上的人把行李一件件搬上船，风从海面吹来，旗子朝同一个方向抖开。 The ship's outward journey took three days.
sceneCN: 这里的 outward 是「向外的、出程的」（第 1 个义项：朝远离中心的方向）；句意为这艘船出航用了三天。图中可辨识物件：行李、船、抖开的旗。

derivatives.zh: 由 outward 加副词性 -s 构成，为英式英语常用的「向外」
由 outward 加 -ly 构成，义为「表面上；向外」

senses.title: Directed away from the centre
senses.definition: pointing or moving away from the inside or the centre of something
senses.definitionCN: 指向或移向某物的外部或远离中心的方向
senses.example: The ship's outward journey took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船出航用了三天。
senses.why: Outward is out plus the old suffix -weard, which means turned towards, so the word describes a thing turned to face away from where it started.
senses.whyCN: outward 是 out 加上古后缀 -weard（朝向），所以这个词描述的是「转过身去、背离起点」的方向。

senses.title: On the surface, not inside
senses.definition: relating to how something looks or appears rather than to what it is really like inside
senses.definitionCN: 指某物看起来的样子，而不是它内里真正的样子
senses.example: Outward calm hid a great deal of worry.
senses.exampleCN: 表面的平静掩藏了大量忧虑。
senses.why: If outward points to the outer side, it can also point to the outer layer of a person, and what lies on that layer is what others see rather than what is felt.
senses.whyCN: 既然 outward 指向外面那一侧，它也能指一个人的外层，而外层上的东西是别人看见的，不是他自己感到的。

senses.title: Belonging to the outside world
senses.definition: concerned with things outside a place, group or country, such as trade with other countries
senses.definitionCN: 指涉及某地、某群体或某国之外的事情，如与他国的贸易
senses.example: The country's outward trade grew faster than its home market.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的对外贸易增长快于国内市场。
senses.why: The same word of direction is used for whatever crosses a boundary towards others, so a country's dealings with the world outside become outward trade.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表方向的词也用来指越过边界、朝向他人的活动，于是一个国家与外部世界的往来就成了「对外贸易」。

senses.title: Away from the inside, used as an adverb
senses.definition: used as an adverb to describe movement away from a centre or away from oneself
senses.definitionCN: 作副词用，描述远离中心或远离自身的移动
senses.example: The doors open outward onto the courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 这些门向外开，通向院子。
senses.why: The adjective and the adverb share one form because the old suffix could end either kind of word, and English has kept both uses without adding anything.
senses.whyCN: 形容词与副词共用同一个形式，因为那个古老后缀既能构成形容词也能构成副词，英语把两种用法都留下来，没有再添加成分。

intro.en: Outward goes back to an Old English compound of ūt, out, and the suffix -weard, turned towards; English has kept it as both adjective and adverb, with the British adverb often written outwards.
intro.cn: outward 上溯古英语中由 ūt（向外）与后缀 -weard（朝向）构成的复合词；英语让它兼作形容词与副词，英式英语的副词常写作 outwards。

items.en: Ūt meant out, and it marked position or movement away from the inside of something.
items.cn: ūt 意为向外，标出远离某物内部的位置或移动。

items.en: The suffix -weard meant turned towards, and it also built words such as hāmweard, homeward.
items.cn: 后缀 -weard 意为「朝向」，也构成 hāmweard（向家）这类词。

items.en: Ūtweard described something turned or directed outward, and it worked as both adjective and adverb.
items.cn: ūtweard 形容朝外转或朝外指的东西，兼作形容词与副词。

items.en: Middle English kept the word for direction and extended it to the visible surface of a person or thing.
items.cn: 中古英语保留它的方向义，并扩展到一个人或一件东西可见的表面。

items.en: Modern English adds the social sense of outward-looking, and British usage often writes the adverb as outwards.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上 outward-looking 这种对外关注的社会义，英式用法常把副词写作 outwards。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words formed on the same -ward pattern; the near-meaning group collects words for what belongs to the outside or to appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收按 -ward 这一模式构成的词；近义组收表示「属于外部」或「属于表面」的词。

entries.definition: The British adverb form, meaning away from the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 英式副词形式，意为向外。

entries.definition: As it appears on the surface, whatever the truth inside.
entries.definitionCN: 就表面看来，不论内里如何。

entries.definition: Directed towards the inside, or felt privately inside.
entries.definitionCN: 朝向内部的，或内心感受到的。

entries.definition: On the way back towards home.
Belonging to or coming from the outside.
The outer surface of something, or outer.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的外表面，或指外部的。

entries.definition: Further from the centre than something else.
entries.definitionCN: 比另一物离中心更远的。

entries.definition: Seeming true from what can be seen, though possibly not so.
entries.definitionCN: 从可见之处看似为真，但未必如此。

normalIntro.en: Outward is a direction word with an old suffix welded to it, so its hooks follow the line from an inside towards an outside.
normalIntro.cn: outward 是一个焊着古老后缀的方向词，记忆钩子顺着「从里面指向外面」的那条线走。

normal.en: Outward is out plus the old suffix -weard, turned towards, the same suffix that gives toward and homeward.
normal.cn: outward 是 out 加古后缀 -weard（朝向），toward 与 homeward 也出自同一个后缀。

normal.en: Because that suffix could mark either an adjective or an adverb, outward works in both jobs without changing shape.
normal.cn: 正因为那个后缀既能标形容词也能标副词，outward 不用改形就能兼任两职。

normal.en: British English adds -s for the adverb outwards, while American English usually keeps outward for both.
normal.cn: 英式英语给副词加 -s 写成 outwards，而美式英语通常两种用法都用 outward。

normal.en: An outward journey is the trip away from home; the trip back is the return journey.
normal.cn: an outward journey 是离家外出的那一段行程；回程则叫 the return journey。

normal.en: Outwardly adds -ly to mean on the surface, which is why an outwardly calm person may be far from calm.
normal.cn: outwardly 加 -ly 表示「表面上」，所以一个表面上镇定的人可能一点也不镇定。

abstract.en: A word about direction keeps reminding us that the same thing has an outside for other people and an inside for itself.
abstract.cn: 一个关于方向的词反复提醒人：同一件东西，对别人有外面，对自己有里面。

abstract.en: To be outward-looking is to turn the gaze away from one's own affairs, and the word makes that choice a direction rather than a virtue.
abstract.cn: 说一个人对外关注，就是把目光从自己的事务上移开，而这个词把这种选择说成一个方向，而不是一种美德。

abstract.en: Outward calm is not exactly a lie; it is the part of feeling that has been arranged for other people to see.
abstract.cn: 表面的平静并不完全是谎话；它只是感情里被整理好、供别人看的那一部分。

examples.en: The ship's outward journey took three days.
examples.cn: 这艘船出航用了三天。

examples.en: Outward calm hid a great deal of worry.
examples.cn: 表面的平静掩藏了大量忧虑。

examples.en: The doors open outward onto the courtyard.
examples.cn: 这些门向外开，通向院子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特沃德」——奥特转过身朝外面走；记住 outward 是向外的、外表的。

root: 由古英语 ūt（向外）加后缀 -weard（朝向）构成，古英语已写作 ūtweard；同族词有 inward、toward、homeward 等；-weard 属日耳曼语成分，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line drawn from inside to outside; the senses divide into direction, visible surface, dealings with the wider world, and the adverb of movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从内到外的一条线；义项按「方向」「可见的表面」「与外部世界的往来」「表示移动的副词」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat turned inside out, lining inwards, cloth facing the wind, the wind passing over that outer face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件外套被翻过来，里子朝内，布面朝外，风从那一面吹过去。

branches.en: a ship leaving the harbour at dawn
branches.cn: 清晨离港的一艘船

branches.en: a face that shows nothing of the worry
branches.cn: 不露忧虑的一张脸

branches.en: goods crossing a border towards buyers
branches.cn: 越过边境运往买主的货物

branches.en: a door swinging away from the room
branches.cn: 朝房间外推开的一扇门

branches.en: surface and direction share one form
branches.cn: 表面与方向共用一个形式

intro.en: The word is a direction adverb with an old suffix meaning turned towards, and English uses the single form for both adjective and adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是方向副词加上意为「朝向」的古老后缀，英语让同一个形式兼作形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Outward is built from Old English ūt and -weard, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this formation.
latinIntro.cn: outward 由古英语 ūt 与 -weard 构成，这一构词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 捏；掐；夹痛；一撮；匮乏
definition_en: to squeeze skin or a small object tightly between the thumb and a finger, the tiny amount held that way, or a painful shortage of money or time
core_image: 拇指与食指合拢，夹住手臂上一小片皮肤，皮肤被提起一道浅浅的褶
scene: 厨房里盐罐快见底了，母亲用两根手指从罐底夹起最后一点白色颗粒，抖进正在冒泡的汤里。 She added a pinch of salt to the soup and tasted it again.
sceneCN: 这里 pinch 指「一撮」（第 2 个义项：两指夹住的一点点分量）；句意为她往汤里加了一撮盐，又尝了一次。图中可辨识物件：快空的盐罐、两指间的盐粒、冒泡的汤锅。

由 pinch 加 -ed 构成，义为「消瘦憔悴的；拮据的」

senses.title: To squeeze something between finger and thumb
senses.definition: to press a person's skin or a small object tightly between the thumb and another finger
senses.definitionCN: 用拇指与另一根手指把皮肤或小物件紧紧夹住
senses.example: She pinched the bridge of her nose and sighed.
senses.exampleCN: 她捏着鼻梁叹了口气。
senses.why: The word began as a name for a small, sharp bite or nip, so the first sense is a quick two-finger grip rather than a full-handed hold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指轻而尖的一下咬或掐，所以第一个义项是两根手指的短促夹合，而不是整只手握住。

senses.title: A very small amount held between the fingers
senses.definition: a quantity of something, especially a powder, that can be held between the thumb and forefinger
senses.definitionCN: 能用拇指与食指夹住的少量东西，尤指粉末
senses.example: Add a pinch of pepper to the sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 往酱汁里加一撮胡椒。
senses.why: Once the gesture has a name, the amount that the gesture carries is named by the same word, which is why cooks measure salt in pinches rather than in grams.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作一旦有了名字，动作所携带的分量也就用同一个词来称呼，所以厨师用「一撮」而不是用克来量盐。

senses.title: A painful shortage of money or time
senses.definition: a period when money, time, or supplies are so short that people feel pressure
senses.definitionCN: 钱、时间或物资短缺到让人感到压力的时期
senses.example: Like most students, he felt the pinch in the last week of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 和大多数学生一样，他在月底最后一周感到了手头拮据。
senses.why: A pinch is a tight squeeze on the skin; moved onto a household budget, the same squeeze becomes the pressure of having too little, so a physical grip turns into an economic one.
senses.whyCN: pinch 是皮肤上被紧紧夹住的一下；把它挪到家庭预算上，同样的夹紧就变成「东西太少」的压力，身体的紧箍于是成了经济的紧箍。

intro.en: Pinch reached English from an Old French verb for nipping and nibbling, and behind that verb most dictionaries assume a Vulgar Latin form built on the Latin word for a point.
intro.cn: pinch 来自古法语中表示掐、小口啃的动词，而多数词典认为那个动词背后是一个以拉丁语「点、刺」为基础构建的俗拉丁语形式。

items.en: Old French pincier meant to pinch, bite, or nibble, and Middle English borrowed it as pinchen in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 pincier 意为捏、咬、小口啃，中古英语在十四世纪把它借入，写作 pinchen。

items.en: Most dictionaries trace the French verb to a reconstructed Vulgar Latin pinctiare, but that form is not recorded anywhere, so this step is only a generally accepted guess.
items.cn: 多数词典把法语动词追溯到重构的俗拉丁语 pinctiare，但这个形式没有任何文献记录，所以这一步只是被普遍接受的推测。

items.en: Latin punctum meant a point or a prick, and the brief, sharp contact of two fingertips fits that image closely.
items.cn: 拉丁语 punctum 意为「点、刺」，两指尖短促而尖的一下接触，与这个意象相当吻合。

items.en: Middle English pinche(n) kept the bodily action and also began to name the small quantity held in the fingers.
items.cn: 中古英语 pinche(n) 保留了身体动作义，同时开始指用手指夹住的那一点点分量。

items.en: Modern English stretches the squeeze onto money and time, so a family can feel the pinch without anyone touching them.
items.cn: 现代英语把这股挤压延伸到金钱与时间上，于是一家人不必真被谁捏一下，也能「感到拮据」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same nipping image or on the same spelling; the near-meaning group gathers other words for gripping, biting and shortage.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个「夹、刺」意象上的词以及拼写相近的词；近义组收其他表示夹、咬与短缺的词。

entries.definition: To hit hard with a fist; it is often traced to the same Latin idea of a sharp point.
entries.definitionCN: 用拳头重击；它也常被追溯到同一个表示「尖点」的拉丁观念。

entries.definition: A tool with two hinged arms for gripping and pulling.
entries.definitionCN: 两臂铰接、用来夹住并拔出的工具；钳子。

entries.definition: Thin and pale, as if the face had been squeezed.
entries.definitionCN: 消瘦苍白的，仿佛脸被捏过一样。

entries.definition: A small cushion for holding pins; it is built on pin rather than on this word, so the resemblance is only in spelling.

normalIntro.en: The word comes from an Old French verb for nipping, and its family keeps returning to small, sharp contact and to the pressure of having too little.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自古法语中表示掐、咬的动词，它的词族反复回到「短促而尖的接触」以及「东西太少的压力」。

normal.en: Old French pincier meant to nibble as well as to pinch, so the word has always carried a hint of teeth as well as fingers.
normal.cn: 古法语 pincier 既指掐也指小口啃，所以这个词一直带着一点牙齿的意味，而不只是手指。

normal.en: Pincers is the same family with a tool suffix: the thing that does the pinching for you.
normal.cn: pincers 是同一词族加上表工具的后缀，指的是替你去夹的那样东西。

normal.en: A pinch of salt is not a weight but a gesture, which is why recipes leave the exact amount to the cook.
normal.cn: 一撮盐不是重量而是一个动作，所以菜谱把准确分量留给做饭的人自己拿捏。

normal.en: Pinched cheeks look as if someone had squeezed them thin, so the adjective came to mean drawn and pale.
normal.cn: 憔悴的脸颊像是被人捏得没了肉，于是这个形容词就表示「消瘦苍白」。

normal.en: Feel the pinch turns the finger squeeze into the pressure of a tight budget, and the original image survives intact.
normal.cn: feel the pinch 把手指的挤压变成紧巴巴的预算压力，原先的意象原封不动地保留下来。

abstract.en: A pinch is the smallest grip there is: not a hold, only a reminder that something is held.
abstract.cn: 「一捏」是最小的抓握：不算握住，只提醒你某样东西正被拿在手里。

abstract.en: The same word measures salt, squeezes skin and describes a hard month, because all three are pressure applied to something small.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量盐、又掐皮肤、还形容难熬的一个月，因为三者都是施加在小东西上的压力。

abstract.en: English trusts the hand more than the scale: a cook who says a pinch is measuring with a gesture.
abstract.cn: 英语更信任手而不是秤：说「一撮」的厨师，是用一个动作在量分量。

examples.cn: 她捏着鼻梁叹了口气。

examples.cn: 往酱汁里加一撮胡椒。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small, sharp contact of two fingertips; from that gesture come the tiny amount carried in the fingers and the pressure of a budget squeezed too tight.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两指尖短促而尖的一下接触；由这个动作长出指间所夹的一点点分量，以及被夹得过紧的预算压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two fingertips closing on a small fold of skin or on the last grains of salt.
core.cn: 核心意象：拇指与食指合拢，夹住一小片皮肤，或夹住最后几粒盐。

branches.en: a thumb and forefinger closing on the skin of an arm
branches.cn: 拇指与食指在手臂皮肤上合拢

branches.en: a cook shaking the last grains from finger and thumb
branches.cn: 厨师用两指抖下最后几粒盐

branches.en: an empty wallet in the last week of the month
branches.cn: 月底最后一周的空钱包

branches.cn: 先被感觉到、后被告知的一下夹紧

branches.cn: 一家人用一勺一勺来量剩下的东西

senses.title: A small flame
senses.definition: a tiny piece of burning material flying from a fire
senses.definitionCN: 从火中飞出的细小燃烧颗粒

definition_zh: 永久地；永远地；长期地；不可逆地
definition_en: in a way that lasts for a very long time or for ever, in a settled long-term arrangement, or in a way that cannot be undone
core_image: 钉子已经钉进木头，就算拔出来也会留下一个洞
scene: 搬家那天，他把旧钥匙放在桌上，决定不再回来。 The family left the village permanently in the spring.
sceneCN: 这里是「永久地、永远地」（第 1 个义项：长时间不再改变）；句意为这家人春天永久地离开了村子。

pos.zh: 永久地；永远地；长期地；不可逆地

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语 permanens 进入英语，义为「永久的；长期的」
permanent 加名词后缀 -ence，义为「永久性；持久」
permanent 加 -ency，义为「永久；永久的事物」，比 permanence 少见
与 permanent 同出拉丁语 manere（停留），义为「留下；保持」

senses.title: For ever, not for a short time
senses.definition: in a way that lasts for ever, or for the whole period being considered, rather than a short while
senses.definitionCN: 以一种永远持续、或在所考虑的整个期间都持续的方式，而不是短时间
senses.example: The old cinema closed permanently last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老电影院去年冬天永久关闭了。
senses.why: Per- adds the idea of through to manere, to remain, so the word starts from remaining all the way through instead of stopping partway.
senses.whyCN: per- 给 manere（停留）加上了「贯穿到底」的意思，所以这个词的起点是一直留到最后，而不是半途停下。

senses.title: As a settled, long-term arrangement
senses.definition: in a fixed and lasting arrangement, rather than in a temporary or trial position
senses.definitionCN: 以固定的、长久有效的安排，而不是临时或试用的状态
senses.example: After two years on short contracts, he was finally employed permanently.
senses.exampleCN: 签了两年短期合同之后，他终于被长期聘用。
senses.why: Once the word names what does not stop, it also describes arrangements meant to stay in place, so a job or a home can be held permanently.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指「不停下来的东西」，它也能指有意长期维持的安排，于是一份工作或一处住所都可以被长期保有。

senses.title: Irreversibly, with no way back
senses.definition: in a way that cannot be undone or reversed, so the earlier state is gone for good
senses.definitionCN: 以无法撤销或逆转的方式，先前的状态从此消失
senses.example: The flood permanently changed the shape of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那场洪水永久地改变了这条河的走向。
senses.why: Something that remains to the very end leaves no point at which it could be turned back, which is why the word also marks damage or change that can never be repaired.
senses.whyCN: 一件事一直持续到最后，就没有留下任何可以回头的时刻，所以这个词也用来标记再也修不回来的损坏或改变。

intro.en: Permanently is an English adverb built on a Latin verb of remaining: a prefix of through, a verb meaning to stay, and a suffix of manner.
intro.cn: permanently 是建立在拉丁语「停留」动词上的英语副词：一个表示「贯穿」的前缀、一个意为「停留」的动词，加一个表示方式的后缀。

items.en: Latin manere meant to stay or to remain, and it is the source of several English words about staying put.
items.cn: 拉丁语 manere 意为「停留、留下」，是若干表示「待着不动」的英语词的来源。

items.en: The prefix per- added the sense of through, giving permanere, to remain to the end or to endure.
items.cn: 前缀 per- 补上「贯穿」的意思，构成 permanere，意为「留到最后、持续下去」。

items.en: The present participle permanens, with the stem permanent-, described something that keeps on remaining.
items.cn: 现在分词 permanens 的词干为 permanent-，用来形容一直停留、持续存在的东西。

items.en: English took permanent from Latin and French, at first as an adjective meaning lasting or unchanged.
items.cn: 英语经拉丁语与法语借入 permanent，最初作形容词，意为「持久的、不变的」。

items.en: The adverb added -ly to permanent, and it now covers for ever, for the long term, and beyond repair.
items.cn: 副词形式在 permanent 后加 -ly，如今覆盖「永远」「长期」与「无法修复」三种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin verb of remaining; the near-meaning group collects expressions for time without an end.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「停留」动词上的词；近义组收表示「没有终点的时间」的说法。

normalIntro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「停留」动词加上一个表示「贯穿」的前缀，再变成表示方式的副词。

normal.en: Per- means through and manere means to remain, so the pair says to remain through to the end.
normal.cn: per- 意为「贯穿」，manere 意为「停留」，两者合起来就是「一直留到最后」。

normal.en: Permanent is the adjective, and -ly turns it into the adverb without changing the meaning.
normal.cn: permanent 是形容词，加 -ly 变成副词，意思并不改变。

normal.en: Remain and remnant come from the same Latin verb manere, which is why they feel related.
normal.cn: remain 与 remnant 同出拉丁语动词 manere，所以它们读起来有亲缘感。

normal.en: The natural opposite is temporarily, and most collocations set the two against each other.
normal.cn: 它天然的反义词是 temporarily，多数搭配都把两者对立起来。

normal.en: Permanently deleted and permanently closed both mean there is no undo button.
normal.cn: permanently deleted 与 permanently closed 都意味着没有撤销键。

abstract.en: Picture a nail driven flush into wood: even if you pull it out, the hole stays and the surface is never flat again.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚钉子被敲得与木面齐平：就算拔出来，洞还在，表面再也平不回去。

abstract.en: The word is a door with its key thrown away, which is why it fits damage better than it fits furniture.
abstract.cn: 这个词像一扇把钥匙扔掉的门，所以它更适合形容损坏，而不适合形容家具。

abstract.en: Two ideas share one word: time that does not end, and a decision that does not turn back.
abstract.cn: 两种想法共用一个词：不会结束的时间，和不会回头的决定。

examples.en: The library is permanently closed for repairs.
examples.cn: 图书馆因维修永久关闭。

examples.en: She moved permanently to the coast after retiring.
examples.cn: 退休后她永久搬到了海边。

examples.en: The injury left him permanently unable to lift his arm.
examples.cn: 那次受伤让他再也抬不起手臂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼墨能特利」——墨泼到纸上就再也收不回，一泼便是永久；记住 permanently 是永久地。

root: 拉丁语 permanere（持续停留）的现在分词 permanens（词干 permanent-）进入英语作 permanent，再加 -ly 构成；per-（贯穿）加 manere（停留）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is remaining all the way to the end; the senses then split into endless time, settled arrangements and changes that cannot be undone.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一直留到最后；义项由此分为没有尽头的时间、长期固定的安排，以及无法撤销的改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nail driven flush into wood, leaving a hole that never closes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚钉子被敲进木头，留下一个再也合不上的洞。

branches.en: a cinema with its shutters down for good
branches.cn: 卷帘门永远拉下的电影院

branches.en: a key left on a table after moving day
branches.cn: 搬家后留在桌上的钥匙

branches.en: a contract with no end date
branches.cn: 没有截止日期的合同

branches.en: a river bed cut into a new shape
branches.cn: 被冲出全新走向的河床

branches.en: a scar that stays after the cut heals
branches.cn: 伤口愈合后仍留下的疤

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of staying under a prefix of through, then an English adverb ending that marks manner.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「停留」动词加上「贯穿」前缀，再加英语中标记方式的副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: All of the core pieces are Latin: the prefix per-, the verb manere, and the participle permanens.
latinIntro.cn: 核心部件全部来自拉丁语：前缀 per-、动词 manere，以及分词 permanens。

definition_zh: 单数的；奇特的；非凡的
definition_en: relating to one thing in grammar, unusual, or remarkable
core_image: 一个单独的词形在语法表中被圈出
scene: 这个名词的复数形式和单数形式相同。 The plural of this noun looks the same as the singular.
sceneCN: 这里 singular 是「单数」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个名词的复数形式和单数形式相同。

senses.title: The grammar of one
senses.definition: the form of a word used for one person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用于指一个人或一件事的词形
senses.example: The plural of this noun looks the same as the singular.
senses.exampleCN: 这个名词的复数形式和单数形式相同。
senses.why: This is the schoolroom sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是课堂上最常用的义项。

senses.title: Unusual or strange
senses.definition: not ordinary or common
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常或不常见的
senses.example: There was a singular smell in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里有一股奇特的气味。
senses.why: Something one of a kind feels strange.
senses.whyCN: 独一无二之物会显得奇特。

senses.title: Remarkable
senses.definition: very great or outstanding
senses.definitionCN: 非常杰出或卓越的
senses.example: She showed singular courage in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 她在风暴中表现出非凡的勇气。
senses.why: The same one-of-a-kind sense turns to praise.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「独一无二」也可转为赞美。

intro.en: Singular comes from a Latin word for single.
intro.cn: singular 来自拉丁语中表示「单个」的词。

items.en: Singularis meant single or alone.
items.cn: singularis 意为单个的或单独的。

items.en: Singulier kept the grammatical sense.
items.cn: singulier 保留了语法含义。

items.en: English borrowed it for grammar and oddity.
items.cn: 英语借入它表示语法和奇特。

items.en: It also came to mean remarkable.
items.cn: 它也获得了「非凡」之义。

items.en: It is a common label in grammar books.
items.cn: 它成为语法书中的常见标签。

note.en: Singular is compared with similar-looking words and words for unusual.
note.cn: 把 singular 与形近词以及表示不寻常的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Singular starts in grammar and reaches toward one of a kind.
normalIntro.cn: singular 从语法出发，延伸到「独一无二」。

normal.en: The plural of this noun looks the same as the singular.
normal.cn: 这个名词的复数形式和单数形式相同。

normal.en: It was a singular moment in her life.

abstract.en: One of a kind is both strange and precious.
abstract.cn: 独一无二既显得奇特，也显得珍贵。

abstract.en: Grammar counts, but singular reminds us that one can shine.
abstract.cn: 语法在数数，而 singular 提醒我们「一」也能闪耀。

abstract.en: A singular thing has no copy.
abstract.cn: 独特之物没有副本。

examples.en: She showed singular courage in the storm.

dict_mnemonic.text: single（单一的）+ -ar = singular；语法里指「单数」，日常里指「奇特、非凡」，都由「独一无二」引申而来。

root: 源自拉丁语 singularis（单个的、独特的），经古法语 singulier 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Singular means the grammar of one, unusual, or remarkable.
sensesIntro.cn: singular 意为语法上的单数、奇特的或非凡的。

core.en: One that stands apart from the many.
core.cn: 从众多之中单独站出的一个。

branches.en: A grammar table marks the form for one.
